name: Jamison Moorehead
fact: The Senate elected him Sustainability Committee chair on 25 February 2020, unanimously, on the recommendation of Leslie North, director of WKU's Office of Sustainability. He was a freshman at the time. The same meeting confirmed five new senators and a second committee chair, Kat Howard for SAVES.

src.label: College Heights Herald, 26 Feb 2020, "SGA confirms 5 senators, 4 voted in unanimously", by Brody Rexing; the recommendation and his year are in the photograph caption, the meeting account in the article.

name: Parker Raybourne
fact: Confirmed as a senator on 25 February 2020, the only one of the five nominees that night not voted in unanimously. He had served previously on the Academic and Student Affairs committee, wrote no legislation in that time, and had spent the previous semester at Harlaxton College in England. Senators questioned his qualifications and, briefly, his membership of WKU College Republicans, which he confirmed; Speaker Nathan Terrell cut that line of questioning off as inappropriate and reminded the chamber that SGA is non-partisan.

src.label: College Heights Herald, 26 Feb 2020, "SGA confirms 5 senators, 4 voted in unanimously", by Brody Rexing.

name: Me'Lon Craighead
fact: Among the five senators confirmed at the meeting of 25 February 2020. The Herald prints the surname "Criaghead" in that article, which is a transposition; its own 2022 caption and this archive both have Craighead. Flagged, not fixed.

name: Matt Barr
fact: Was Campus Improvements chair at the meeting of 25 February 2020, and spoke against holding committee-chair nominees to a test of legislation already written, arguing that a committee exists to develop ideas together.

name: Me'Lon Craighead
fact: Serving as executive vice president, she addressed the assembly at SGA's first meeting of 2022, on 18 January 2022 in the Senate Chambers on the second floor of Downing Student Union. The meeting passed a bill to replenish the Office of Sustainability pantry.

src.label: College Heights Herald, 18 Jan 2022, "SGA holds first meeting of 2022, passes bill to replenish office of sustainability pantry"; she is named in the caption of the third of four photographs.

note: QUARANTINED CROP, CONFIRMED AND PUBLISHED - Jamison Moorehead. The file was called 2021-22-jamison-moorehead.jpg, but the photograph it was cut from is dated 26 February 2020, so it is filed at 2019-20, which is one of his years and the year of the Sustainability chairmanship the picture records. It is a crop of the right-hand figure of two men shaking hands; the caption names only Moorehead. The other man is Will Harris, identified by comparing him with the archive's own confirmed 2019-20-will-harris.jpg, and the article names Harris as president, so the younger figure being congratulated is Moorehead. A sliver of Harris's red sleeve survives at the crop's right edge, which is what proves the crop came from that frame rather than a lookalike. Removed from _unverified.

QUARANTINED CROP, CONFIRMED AND PUBLISHED - Me'Lon Craighead. Cut from the third of four photographs run with the Herald's 18 January 2022 meeting story; only that one of the four names anybody, and it names only her. She is the sole figure standing and speaking at the podium, the other person in the frame being a seated listener shot from behind. She is masked and in three-quarter profile, so it is a poor portrait, and the finding carries quality:"masked". Nothing better exists: a sweep of every Herald post mentioning Craighead turned up attached photographs on only three of them, and none of the others names her. Removed from _unverified.

CLOBBER HAZARD, ANNE-MARIE WRIGHT - read this before touching her file. Anne-Marie Wright ALREADY has a published, cited portrait at data/photos/2024-25-anne-marie-wright.jpg, 420x684, sourced in data/photos.json to the Herald of 24 September 2024, showing her standing in a black and red SGA polo. The quarantined crop in _unverified carried the SAME filename but is a DIFFERENT PHOTOGRAPH, 620x760: she is standing at the WKU podium in an orange Western Kentucky sweatshirt, both hands raised mid-gesture, an open laptop in front of her and water bottles across the foreground. It is not a re-crop of the published frame. Copying it into data/photos/ under that name would silently destroy the cited portrait. If it is confirmed, it must either replace the existing entry deliberately, with "replaces" set, or be given a different filename. I did not copy it, and the published 420x684 file was still intact when I stood down. The crop had already been taken out of _unverified by another agent by then. My own view of the two: same person beyond doubt, and the podium frame is larger and warmer, but her hands are mid-gesture and her expression is mid-speech, so the published frame is the better portrait of the two. Its source was not established.

LEAD, NOT A CONFIRMATION - Alex Cissell, and there is a trap in it. The quarantined crop 2021-22-alex-cissell.jpg, 1240x1314, is a studio headshot against a mottled brown backdrop: smiling straight at the camera, pale sleeveless knit top, by some distance the most flattering image I saw all night. Its almost certain source is https://wkuherald.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Alex_Cissell_1.jpg, 2001x1334, whose caption reads that Alex Cissell is a member of the Student Publications Advertising Staff for Fall 2023; it hangs off post 72411, which redirects to the Herald staff page https://wkuherald.com/staff_name/alex-cissell/. THE TRAP: that caption identifies a Herald advertising staffer, not the SGA committee chair, and CLAUDE.md forbids merging two people on a shared name. The link that closes the gap is the other Cissell photograph, https://wkuherald.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/6Y9A0080.jpg, 2001x1440, captioned as WKU senior public relations student Alex Cissell on the left with SGA Senator at Large Sophia Bryant on the right, describing Bill 36-23-S during an SGA meeting. If the face in the studio headshot is the face of the left-hand figure there, the headshot depicts a person the Herald puts inside SGA business, and it can be published; if not, it cannot. I could not download either file to make that comparison. Do that comparison before publishing the headshot.

NOT INSPECTED - 2022-23-aniya-johnson.jpg (749 KB, 1667x2500) and 2022-23-preston-romanov.jpg (215 KB, 1171x1001) were still in _unverified when I stood down and I never opened either. 2022-23-olivia-feck.jpg had already been taken by another agent. Nothing I did bears on any of the three.

TECHNIQUE THAT PAID - where a caption names one person but the frame holds two, the archive's own confirmed portraits will often identify the other one and settle it by elimination. That is how Moorehead was pinned down: the bearded man in the red windbreaker was matched against data/photos/2019-20-will-harris.jpg, and once he is Harris, and the article calls Harris president, the caption's single named subject has to be the other figure. Worth trying before rejecting any two-person frame.

SOURCE ACCESS, STATE AT HANDOVER - wkuherald.com was returning Cloudflare 403 to every non-browser client on this machine by about 23:10, the whole host including /wp-json and /wp-content, and it had not lifted forty minutes later. curl with browser headers, curl with its own default headers, HTTP/1.1, python urllib and node fetch all got the same 403, so it is keyed to the address rather than to a TLS fingerprint, and no amount of backoff helped. Only the real Chrome session still worked. Three further dead ends, recorded so nobody repeats them: Chrome permits exactly one blob download per origin before it starts blocking automatic downloads, and wkuherald.com is now in that blocked state, so a.download stops working after the first file; base64 returned through the browser tool is refused by the harness with "[BLOCKED: Base64 encoded data]", so bytes cannot be carried out that way; and neither of the two images I wanted has any Wayback snapshot, so the Internet Archive is not a mirror for these. The route the fleet has settled on, scripts/chrome/chromechunk.js over the DevTools protocol, is the one to use.

SEARCH TRAP - the Herald media endpoint returns newest first and caps a page at a hundred, so a bare name search drowns in 2026 photographs and looks empty for older years. Add order=asc, or search data/herald-photos.json locally. Separately, and this matters as much: caption search alone misses people who are pictured but described only by office. Search the posts endpoint for the name, then list the media attached to each post that comes back with /wp-json/wp/v2/media?parent=<post id>. That is how the only two frames naming Craighead were found.
